messages:
Maria (CS): Hey team, GammaFin is hitting p99 spikes since ~10:05 UTC, complaining about tail latency for text-generation API. They sent a couple request IDs: req=gf-9921, gf-9927. They say p95 ok but p99 up to ~2.8s (was ~400ms before). Can someone triage?

Todd (SRE): Thanks Maria. Can you paste a sample trace/span id? Also is this across regions or just us-east-1?

Maria (CS): They included a trace id in the support ticket: trace=0a3f7c. Affected region is us-east-1 only (customer sits there). They also said it started after a scheduled deploy at 09:58.

Anish (Infra): grabbing logs. Running quick query on tail latencies for tenant gammafin (tenant_id=gf-001) across the modelpool.

Anish (Infra): quick findings: overall cluster p99 unchanged, but gf-001 p99 spikes line up with GPU node gpu-3@pool-a saturating. GPU utilization jumps to 98% at the same times.

Todd (SRE): that smells like noisy neighbor or tenant hot-spot. Any per-tenant routing/allowlist that could be forcing them to a larger model variant? @Phil?

Phil (Support): Maria says they were moved to a new allowlist yesterday to enable 'gptx-16k' for longer contexts. Could that push them to a heavier kernel? :thinking_face:

Anish (Infra): yep. I pulled routing decision logs: requests for gf-001 are routed to model variant gptx-16k-qa when len>2048. The QA variant has heavier compute path and the pool only has limited capacity. Example routing line: 

```
2026-05-22T10:05:13Z route_id=rt-71 tenant=gf-001 model=gptx-16k-qa pool=pool-a node=gpu-3 decision=allowlist
```

Todd (SRE): So per-tenant allowlist enabled larger model -> bumped into capacity limits -> noisy neighbor -> tail latency. Two mitigation paths: 1) immediate: override routing for gf-001 to a lower-CPU variant or route to another pool; 2) medium: spin up more capacity / move tenant to dedicated pool.

Maria (CS): Customer is on standard plan, not Dedicated. They'll accept a temporary routing change if it fixes latency. They asked for a patch within the hour if possible.

Anish (Infra): I can push a temporary routing override to force gptx-8k for gf-001. Command I will run: 

```
redwoodctl routing override set --tenant gf-001 --model gptx-8k --ttl 3600 --reason "temp mitigate p99 spikes"
```

Todd (SRE): Also let's check per-tenant throttles. If they burst and we don't throttle, they can monopolize KV caches and batching slots, worsening p99. Run a voucher on token churn.

Anish (Infra): ran a quick throttle check: gf-001 had several high-concurrency bursts (concurrency=48) while typical is 6-12. That explains jitter. I'm initiating two actions: 1) apply routing override, 2) set soft concurrency cap for gf-001 to 24 with gradual backoff. Applying now.

deploy-bot: deploy started: routing-override/gf-001 -> gptx-8k (initiated by Anish).

deploy-bot: deploy ok: routing-override/gf-001 -> gptx-8k (completed at 10:18 UTC).

Anish (Infra): applied soft concurrency cap: 

```
redwoodctl tenant throttle set --tenant gf-001 --max-concurrency 24 --mode soft
```

Maria (CS): I told the customer we made a temporary change and asked them to retry. They responded: "latency looks much better for the last 10 min, p99 back to ~420ms". :thumbsup:

Todd (SRE): Nice. Can we capture before/after metrics for the incident? Put them in the incident ticket. I want p50/p95/p99 for gf-001 and pool-a for the window 09:50-10:30.

Anish (Infra): grabbing metrics. Quick summary: gf-001 p99: 2.8s -> 0.42s after override. pool-a p99 (all tenants): 880ms -> 620ms (pool still a bit noisy). GPU-3 process list showed steady large-kernel ops from gf-001 at spike time.

Phil (Support): Customer asked if we can prevent this happening again short-term without Dedicated. Can we do an allowlist change that keeps their longer-context feature but throttles concurrency or auto-falls back when pool load is high?

Todd (SRE): Yes — implement policy: per-tenant adaptive fallback. If pool load > 85% or GPU queue > X, route tenant to gptx-8k or gptx-4k as fallback. We already have the smart-routing hooks. Recommend TTL 10m for fallback decisions.

Anish (Infra): I'll open a PR to add a new policy 'per-tenant-adaptive-fallback' with config: 

```
- trigger: pool_utilization_pct >= 85
- action: re-route to smaller-variant
- ttl: 600
- priority: tenant_overrides > default
```
I'll also add telemetry to record when fallback triggers for audit.

Maria (CS): Customer appreciated the quick action and asked for a postmortem and a config that doesn't silently change their model. They want an opt-in that shows fallback events via webhooks.

Todd (SRE): Good ask. Add webhook event for 'routing.fallback' with payload {tenant, from_model, to_model, reason, timestamp}. We should also surface fallback count in Console for tenant owners.

Anish (Infra): Logged follow-ups: 1) PR for adaptive fallback (review: @Todd) 2) telemetry + webhook (PR) 3) runbook update for noisy-tenant mitigation 4) ops note: consider recommending Dedicated for high-concurrency long-context workloads.

Maria (CS): I'll send GammaFin a short summary and link them to the runbook and offer a 2-week trial of Dedicated to evaluate predictability.

Todd (SRE): For the incident record: root cause = per-tenant allowlist enabling heavier model variant combined with bursty concurrency -> GPU pool saturation (noisy neighbor) -> p99 regressions. Immediate mitigations: routing override and soft concurrency cap. Longer term: adaptive fallback + webhook + recommend Dedicated.

Phil (Support): marking customer ticket as "mitigated" and will follow up tomorrow with status.

Maria (CS): thanks everyone. I'll close this thread after we have PR links and the postmortem stub.

Anish (Infra): PRs opened: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/432 (adaptive-fallback), github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/217 (fallback-webhook). Adding runbook edits now.

Todd (SRE): leaving a final note: consider adding quota-based backpressure at the API gateway for per-tenant bursts. It helps protect shared pools.

Maria (CS): noted. Closing loop. :white_check_mark:
